summary: deliver() in packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts now publishes the receipt on the reply inbox immediately after renderInbound() returns, under the unchanged guard (reply !== "" && subject === agentSubject(sessionID)), wrapped so a failed publish is logged with the event id and delivery continues; the trailing publish is deleted and nothing else in deliver() moves. Dedupe on dedupe_key is byte-identical. Proven by five envoy.test.ts changes (red recorded before the code change), CI's exact pi-envoy steps, and PR #1083.

trickyParts: The receipt block sits after renderInbound() and before the subscriptionRemovedTopics loop: a frame renderInbound throws on is still never acknowledged (spec Errors row 1), and the receipt precedes the dedupe check, the inbox update, armAskReminder (workspace base only; removed on main by #1074), postDispatchReply, askEphemeral, and sendMessage.
Exactly one `.publish(reply)` remains in envoy.ts; no new import (agentSubject and ensureConnection already existed); the dedupeKeys.add block is byte-identical.
The fixture's publish mock gained onPublish (ordered recording) and failPublishes (throw once); afterEach resets both.

gh probes the cwd's .git and the workspace's colocated gitdir points at a stale /home/ubuntu/... worktree path, so `legion gh -- pr create` had to run from /tmp with explicit --repo/--head/--base (no repository read needed).
deviations: Red was 5 fail / 0 pass, not the plan's 4 fail / 1 pass: test 1c (dedupe) also failed pre-fix because the third receipt `_INBOX.next` had not been published when sendMessage resolved the awaited promise — i.e. it observes the old ack-after-injection order too and is deterministic under the new order. Kept as written; it pins the contract LEGION-107 relies on.
